Class NestedJarFile

java.lang.Object
java.util.zip.ZipFile
java.util.jar.JarFile
io.micronaut.runner.NestedJarFile
All Implemented Interfaces:
Closeable, AutoCloseable
public final class NestedJarFile extends JarFile
A JarFile view of one nested jar of a runner archive, served entirely from the index.

Libraries that scan the class path do it through JarFile: Flyway looks for migrations, Liquibase for change logs, Micronaut for service metadata, and every one of them enumerates entries and opens streams rather than asking a class loader. A nested jar is not a file, so it cannot be opened as one; this class answers those questions from the index instead, which is both faster and free of the temporary files the JDK would otherwise write.

Why it extends JarFile at all

The type is what libraries accept, so the view has to be a JarFile. The constructor hands the super class the outer archive, with verification off and at the base version, so that the JDK reuses the cached ZipFile.Source of a file it has very likely opened already rather than opening and parsing a second one. Every accessor is then overridden to answer for the nested jar.

The two methods that cannot be corrected

JarFile.isMultiRelease() and JarFile.getVersion() are final. They keep reporting the state of the outer archive, which is not multi-release and is opened at the base version, even when this view is of a multi-release dependency. This is a genuine, documented limitation, and it is only a reporting one: getEntry(String) applies the nested jar's own multi-release policy, so lookups still return the versioned entry a real JarFile would return, and NestedJarEntry.getRealName() still reports the META-INF/versions/<n>/... name it came from. Code that branches on isMultiRelease() rather than on the entry it gets back will take the base branch and still be handed versioned entries.

Enumeration

entries(), stream() and size() report the physical records of the jar in central directory order: the versioned aliases and the synthesised directory records the index adds are left out, so a scan sees the same entries, in the same order and in the same number, as it would see in the original dependency. getEntry(String) does include a synthesised directory, because a lookup of some/package/ is a question about the jar's content and the answer "yes, that directory exists" is the useful one.

  • Constructor Details

    • NestedJarFile

      public NestedJarFile(File outerFile, Index index, ArchiveSource source, int jarId) throws IOException
      Opens a view of one nested jar.

      The outer file is opened through the super class only so that this object is a usable JarFile; none of its content is read through it.

      Parameters:
      outerFile - the outer runner archive
      index - the index of that archive
      source - the reader of that archive
      jarId - the nested jar, which must not be the application layer
      Throws:
      IOException - if the outer archive cannot be opened
      IllegalArgumentException - if jarId is not a nested jar of the index

    • getEntry

      public ZipEntry getEntry(String entryName)
      Looks an entry up by its logical name, honouring the nested jar's own multi-release policy.

      As ZipFile does, a name that does not resolve and does not end with a slash is retried with one, so that getEntry("some/package") finds the directory entry.

      Overrides:
      getEntry in class JarFile
      Parameters:
      entryName - the entry name relative to this jar
      Returns:
      the entry, or null when this jar has no such entry

    • stream

      public Stream<JarEntry> stream()
      The physical entries of this jar, in central directory order.

      This is one of the few places in the launcher that touches java.util.stream: the method is inherited from JarFile and has to be overridden, or a caller would be handed the outer archive's entries. Nothing on the startup path calls it.

      Overrides:
      stream in class JarFile
      Returns:
      a stream of the entries

    • getInputStream

      public InputStream getInputStream(ZipEntry entry) throws IOException
      Opens the content of an entry of this jar, straight out of the archive.

      An entry this view produced is served from the record it already carries; any other entry is looked up by name first, so that a caller that kept a ZipEntry of its own still works.

      Overrides:
      getInputStream in class JarFile
      Parameters:
      entry - the entry to read
      Returns:
      the content, or null when this jar has no such entry, as ZipFile does
      Throws:
      IOException - if the archive no longer agrees with the index or the entry cannot be read

    • getManifest

      public Manifest getManifest() throws IOException
      The manifest of the nested jar, parsed on first use and then kept.

      The entry is looked up even when the index's has-manifest flag is clear: it costs one hash probe once per jar, and a stale flag would otherwise strip a library of its Implementation-Version and its package sealing without a trace.

      Overrides:
      getManifest in class JarFile
      Returns:
      the manifest, or null when the jar has none
      Throws:
      IOException - if the manifest cannot be read or is malformed

    • close

      public void close()
      Does nothing.

      Views are shared: one instance per nested jar serves every library in the process, so a library that closes the JarFile it was handed, and several do, must not take the jar away from the others. The handle on the outer file is released when the launcher releases the archive.

      Specified by:
      close in interface AutoCloseable
      Specified by:
      close in interface Closeable
      Overrides:
      close in class ZipFile
